description: List the HubSpot CRM object types a person can sync: the four standard ones — contacts, companies, deals, tickets — plus every custom object this portal defines. Each option's id is what hubspot-list_records-1 and hubspot-search_records-1 take as object_type. `query` keeps only the types whose label or name contains that text. This is the browse node behind the hubspot sync picker, so its output is the scope-option shape.

parent_id.description: Ignored. Object types are a flat list, so there is nothing to open.

query.description: Keep only object types whose label or name contains this text, ignoring case.

cursor.description: Ignored. The schemas call answers with every custom object in one response.

limit.description: Ignored. The schemas call takes no page size.

next_cursor.description: Always null. HubSpot returns every schema in one answer.

custom_schemas.description: Lenient ingress on GET /crm/v3/schemas. HubSpot sends the whole property and association definition of every custom object here; this reads the three fields the node maps.

quirks: The four standard object types are a static list, not a call. HubSpot has no endpoint that returns contacts, companies, deals and tickets — /crm/v3/schemas answers with CUSTOM objects only — and these four exist in every portal, so declaring them beats inventing a call that cannot be made.

A custom object's id is its objectTypeId, the 2-1234567 form, because a portal can rename an object and the numeric id survives it. HubSpot accepts either form on the object endpoints, and the node falls back to the name when a schema arrives without an objectTypeId.

crm.schemas.custom.read is the scope /crm/v3/schemas needs, and it is the only scope in this app that is not about reading records. A portal with no custom objects still answers, with an empty results array.
The schemas call takes no cursor and no page size. next_cursor is always null and the cursor and limit inputs are accepted and ignored, so one generic picker can call every browse node the same way.
The path is /crm/v3/schemas, HubSpot's documented alias for /crm-object-schemas/v3/schemas. This is the one node in the app whose endpoint is not under /crm/v3/objects/.
